content.comment_body: Hello, is anyone able to provide advice on connecting a microphone ([product_name], model [product_name]) to a [company_name] [product_name] controller? Has anyone had experience connecting a microphone to such a device? Below are the microphone specifications: Model: [product_name] General specifications: coverage area 5-40m2, sensitivity -40dB (adjustable), frequency response 20Hz–20kHz, omni-directional, SNR 70dB (1m), dynamic range 104dB, max sound pressure 120dB SPL, output impedance 600Ω, output signal amplitude 2.5Vpp/-25dB, operating voltage DC 12V, operating current 60mA, and temperature range -30℃ to +70℃. Thank you!
The [product_name] is a PLC and not designed as audio equipment.
I understand this, but I’d like to know if connecting is possible by using extra hardware such as a voltage amplifier or a signal converter for the microphone’s output.

The [product_name] has analog inputs with a 0-10V range. I am unsure if your microphone output is compatible directly. You would need something that transforms the microphone signal to a 0-10V voltage, sustained for at least 300ms, for valid input.
Hello [user_name], Could you please provide more details on your intended application? Sharing specifics may help others suggest alternative solutions. [user_name] (translated with Google)

analysis.insight_summary: Participants are evaluating the possibility of integrating an external microphone with a [company_name] [product_name] controller. The main challenge identified is converting the microphone’s audio output into a voltage level and duration compatible with the controller’s analog inputs. Adapting audio equipment to PLC standards requires additional signal conversion hardware, as the controller is not designed for direct audio processing.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes to learn whether it’s feasible to link a microphone to a [company_name] [product_name] controller, and seeks recommendations regarding additional hardware needed for signal conversion and compatibility.
